heading: Wednesday, August 12, 2026
topLine: 2 stories on AI and open problems: Hadamard matrices of order 668 and OEIS conjectures benchmark. Also: 2 model releases: Alibaba Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and xAI Grok 4.6.

items.headline: Claude-assisted team finds Hadamard matrices for all twelve open orders below 2000
items.summary: Levent Alpöge announced Hadamard matrices of order 668 (the smallest order with no known example) and of the eleven other open orders below 2000. Epoch AI credits the work to a team of three humans working with an internal Claude model. The matrices can be checked directly by computer. Epoch's FrontierMath open-problems page lists the problem as solved (human + AI), but there is no technical paper yet. The Hadamard conjecture itself remains open.

items.headline: Language models settle 147 of 492 open OEIS conjectures in Epoch AI test
items.summary: Tom Adamczewski (Epoch AI) ran general-purpose language models against 492 open OEIS conjectures that a DeepMind team had formalized in Lean. With a $50 budget per attempt, the models produced Lean-checked proofs or disproofs of 147 of them (30%). The results are machine-checked, but most of the conjectures are minor. The paper is an arXiv preprint.

items.headline: Alibaba releases open weights for Qwen3.8-Max-class model
items.summary: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B is the open-weight, text-only version of Qwen3.8-Max (2.4T total, 95B active parameters), released on Hugging Face and ModelScope. Its license requires providers with large annual revenue to obtain a commercial license; Qwen reports 67.7 on SWE-bench Pro.

items.headline: SpaceXAI releases Grok 4.6
items.summary: Grok 4.6 builds on Grok 4.5 with stronger support for long-running agents and visual or interactive projects, at the same $2/$6 per million token pricing. The company reports it matches GPT-5.6 Sol at 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
